blocks.value: Clinical Psychology courses teach skills to understand, study and help people with mental health issues . Popular colleges are JMI, SIMTS, Amity University, SRIHER, etc.
Jobs available for graduates are Psychiatrists, Counsellors, Clinical Psychologists, etc. Recruiters include Mannah Wellness, Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Fortis Hospital, etc.

faqs.question: What qualification is required to become a Clinical Psychologist?
faqs.answer: Things you need to become a clinical psychologist can be different in different countries and colleges, but mostly people follow some steps. Here are normal steps: Bachelor Degree: First you do BSc Psychology, BSc Clinical Psychology, or something similar. Master Degree: After bachelor, people usually do master in Clinical Psychology or something close. Doctor Degree: Most clinical psychologists do doctor degree for full qualification.

faqs.question: Does a Clinical Psychologist need an MBBS degree?
faqs.answer: No, a Clinical Psychologist don’t need MBBS degree. Clinical Psychologists and doctors (MBBS) study different stuff. Doctors go to medical school, do internship and residency, and can treat all kinds of medical problems, even some mental health problems. Clinical Psychologists and Psychiatrists usually work together to help people with mental health problems.

faqs.question: How does the syllabus for Clinical Psychology courses differ across universities in India?
faqs.answer: Syllabus for Clinical Psychology course is different in different colleges in India. It depend on things like how course is made, what special area they focus, and college rules. Core subjects like abnormal psychology, counselling, and testing people’s mind are common, but some colleges teach more about brain stuff, cognitive therapy, or psychoanalysis. Some colleges give lot of practical training, internships, and research, and some focus more on theory. Also, what optional subjects, case studies, or fieldwork you get can be different, so each college syllabus is a bit special.

faqs.question: What are the key areas of study for Clinical Psychology students?
faqs.answer: Students of Clinical Psychology courses study key areas such as abnormal psychology which focuses on mental disorders and their symptoms and also psychological assessment which includes diagnostic tests and evaluation methods. They also learn counselling and psychotherapy techniques covering cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), psychoanalysis and also humanistic approaches. Neuropsychology explores brain's impact on behaviour while developmental psychology examines psychological changes across lifespan.

blocks.value: Clinical P sychology can be defined as a branch of P sychology that diagnoses and treats people with mental illnesses, abnormal behaviour, and other psychiatric issues. It is believed that Lightner Witmer was one of the first psychoanalysts who started Clinical Psychology in 1896.

Psychology is one of the most sought-after career alternatives for students who wish to work for society's benefit and are inclined to help people. A career as a Psychologist provides an opportunity to help people with mental issues and help them lead a normal and non-judgemental life. The students that aim to take up Clinical Psychology as a career choice need to opt for Psychology as a subject in Class 12.
To become a certified Clinical psychologist, a student must obtain a Bachelor's degree, then a Master's degree, and a doctorate in Clinical Psychology.
DFP-Banner
Clinical Psychology Syllabus-Important Facts
Clinical Psychologists are required to identify the mental and emotional issues with the patient and curate a treatment plan that includes personal therapy and medication in some instances.

value: BSc in Clinical Psychology is a three-year undergraduate program me that can be pursued full-time, part-time, or through distance education. To apply for the course, the students must pass the entrance examination conducted online and offline mode. To get admitted to the course, the students need to obtain a required percentage score in the entrance examination. The universities decide on a cut-off every year, which is the percentage required score for that year.

MSc in Clinical Psychology is a two-year post-graduate course divided into four semesters. The students aspiring to pursue the course must have a BSc degree from a reputed college with a minimum of 50 per cent marks.

Doctorate (PhD) in Clinical Psychology is a three-year program divided into six semesters. The students wishing to pursue the program need to pass the qualifying entrance examination; however, students who have cleared the GATE / NET /SET/ MPhil / JRF examinations are exempt and get direct admission.

blocks.value: List of Subjects in Clinical Psychology Syllabus
The Clinical Psychology syllabus is segregated into core subjects and elective subjects. The below tables bring the list of core and elective Clinical Psychology subjects.
Typical core subjects for Clinical Psychology

value: Psychopathology is a study of mental disorders and abnormal behaviour in patients. The main components of the study are: Loss of freedom and inability to understand the alternatives Loss of connection with one’s inner self and the inability to be productive Dissociation with people Mental distress

Community psychology studies the effect of community on people's mental well-being and health and how people form connections within their communities and social circles. The subject enables psychologists to look for disturbing or unpleasant situations in a community and understand their effect on the mental health of its residents. It focuses on several factors such as: Cultural environment Political environment Economic environment International influences

Statistics in Psychology helps students to understand data in a better manner and to reach a definite conclusion. Psychologists can discover patterns and arrive at viable conclusions to help the patients.

Developmental Psychology refers to studying human growth and mental development that includes cognitive, physical, social, and intellectual aspects of human growth. It covers several stages of human development, such as: Healthcare Education Medicine Social work

The subject covers the study of human behaviour and ethical and professional boundaries. Counselling can be various kinds like: Event counselling Performance counselling Professional growth counselling

blocks.value: Typical elective subjects for clinical psychology

value: The subject deals with the psychological study and understanding of people between 60-75. It covers several aspects of their mental capabilities like: Physiological changes Psychological changes Social changes

Sports Psychology covers the mental well-being of sports persons and athletes. It talks about the co-dependency of an athlete's physical and psychological health. The sports psychologist works with the athletes to manage their mental health and the stress associated with the sport.

Health Psychology focuses on the biological, social, and psychological factors affecting the health and fitness of people. It focuses on how some patients manage their illnesses and why some do not follow medical advice.

Cognitive Psychology is also known as the science of the brain. It covers how the brain functions and remembers and recalls essential information. Cognitive psychology includes: Use of language Problem-solving Attention span Perception
Psychological analysis is also known as Psychoanalysis. It is used to understand the person’s inability to learn and understand things.

questions.question_text: What is an MPhil Clinical Psychology?

answers.answer_text: The MPhil Clinical Psychology is a 2-year-long PG research programme where students focus on the application of psychological principles to address mental health challenges. They study subjects like psychopathology, psychotherapy techniques, and ethical considerations in clinical practice. Know more about - MPhil Course

questions.question_text: What are the challenges faced by students in Clinical Psychology programs?

answers.answer_text: The challenges faced by students in Clinical Psychology programs are: Managing heavy coursework and clinical training together Coping with emotionally demanding case studies Developing empathy without burnout Handling ethical dilemmas in practice Balancing theory with real-world application Building confidence during supervised sessions Managing stress from exams and licensure preparation Facing the financial costs of long training programs Limited exposure to diverse clinical populations Pressure to stay updated with evolving research and therapies

questions.question_text: How do Clinical Psychology courses address the integration of mental health and physical health?

answers.answer_text: In Clinical Psychology courses , students learn about psychosomatic conditions, chronic illness management, and the mind-body connection. Training includes collaboration with medical teams and patient counseling. This prepares graduates to consider physical health factors in psychological care, promoting holistic treatment plans that improve overall well-being and patient outcomes.

questions.question_text: How do Clinical Psychology programs support students' professional development?

answers.answer_text: Clinical Psychology courses emphasize ongoing learning, workshops, conferences, and research opportunities. Students receive mentorship, career counseling, and networking guidance. This holistic support encourages self-reflection, skill enhancement, and confidence-building, helping students grow into competent, ethical, and empathetic professionals ready to serve diverse client needs.

questions.question_text: How do Clinical Psychology courses prepare students for working in forensic settings?

answers.answer_text: In Clinical Psychology courses , students explore legal psychology, criminal behavior, and assessment of offenders. They practice evaluating mental fitness, risk assessments, and report writing under supervision. Exposure to court procedures and case studies equips them to provide evidence-based recommendations in legal contexts, ensuring ethical and professional competence.
